edits.anchor: argues for intact social development rather than against it
edits.html: The 4-year set, and global delay Hops on one foot and throws a ball overhand — gross motor · Copies a square and draws a simple stick figure — fine motor · Speaks in sentences that strangers understand and tells stories — language · Plays cooperatively with friends — social · Jumping, imitating a line and combining words — younger skills; having them does not make a 4-year-old normal in that domain · Global developmental delay — significant delay in two or more domains; evaluate for a cause; under age 3, refer for early intervention; from age 3, refer to the school district for a preschool special education evaluation, with speech, physical and occupational therapy. How NBME framed it: the stem gives one skill present and one missing in each domain, and the options grid normal or delayed across three domains.

edits.html:
Salient decoyNormal in all three domains — jumping and combining words are skills of a 2-year-old, so having them does not make a 4-year-old normal
Unchecked attributeGross motor marked normal — he can jump, but a 4-year-old hops on one foot and this boy cannot balance on one
Unchecked attributeFine motor marked normal — imitating a line is not copying a shape; a 4-year-old copies a square, and this boy cannot copy a circle
Unchecked attributeLanguage marked normal — he combines words, but only half his speech is understood; a 4-year-old speaks in sentences strangers understand
edits.note: Q3: one trapline per group of distractors (each wrong row spares at least one domain)

edits.stem: 4-year-old boy at a well-child visit who imitates a straight line but cannot copy a circle, jumps but cannot balance on one foot, and combines words with only half his speech understood; normal examination
edits.answer: Delayed gross motor, fine motor and language
edits.companion: global developmental delay: evaluate for a cause and refer to the school district for a preschool special education evaluation (early intervention is for children under 3)
edits.d1: Delayed gross motor and language, normal fine motor
edits.d2: Normal gross motor, fine motor and language

edits.stem: 4-year-old girl who hops on one foot, copies a square, draws a stick figure and plays cooperatively, but speaks in two-word phrases that strangers rarely understand
edits.companion: one delayed domain; obtain a hearing evaluation

edits.stem: 4-year-old boy who speaks in sentences strangers understand and plays cooperatively with friends, but cannot hop on one foot and cannot copy a circle
edits.companion: two domains delayed: gross motor and fine motor
